summary_en: This Phase III trial compares proton craniospinal irradiation (pCSI) with involved-field radiation therapy (IFRT) in patients with breast cancer or non-small cell lung cancer that has spread to the cerebrospinal fluid (leptomeningeal metastasis). Both treatments are given 5 days a week for a total of 10 days of treatment. The main outcome is not stated; the record lists the trial as Phase III.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase III compara la radioterapia craneoespinal con protones (pCSI) con la radioterapia de campo involucrado (IFRT) en pacientes con cáncer de mama o cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas que se ha diseminado al líquido cefalorraquídeo (metástasis leptomeníngea). Ambos tratamientos se administran 5 días a la semana, por un total de 10 días de tratamiento. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el ensayo es de fase III.
who_for: Breast cancer or non-small cell lung cancer with newly diagnosed leptomeningeal metastasis, confirmed by spinal fluid testing or by imaging and typical symptoms
Considered a candidate for radiation therapy for leptomeningeal metastasis
Karnofsky performance status of 60 or higher
Blood counts, liver tests and heart function within the limits listed in the record (heart function NYHA class II or better)
not_for: Prior radiation to the spinal cord or cauda equina above the dose limits listed
Unstable angina needing hospital care, or heart attack, within the last 3 months
NYHA class III or IV heart disease
Pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an active infection needing IV antibiotics
